title: Ops Utility Orchestration Inspector
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Our oncall and first-line support teams rely on a growing catalog of small operator utilities (short 'playflows') that execute diagnostic and remediation steps. Over the last two quarters we've increased reuse but also introduced subtle failure modes: silent permission errors, mismatched parameter schemas, and divergent telemetry labels that make post-mortem triage expensive. Problem: there is no lightweight way to verify a playflow's runtime plan before granting it to frontline users, and automation can execute paths that are not instrumented or are missing idempotency guarantees. Proposal: build an 'Inspector' service and CLI that validates and simulates playflows (taskified admin utilities) prior to promotion. The Inspector performs static checks, dry-run sandbox simulations, execution-plan linting (including KV/side-effect annotation checks), RBAC surface analysis, and telemetry label consistency enforcement. It will integrate with the existing task catalog and the ops telemetry plane so that failures are surfaced as actionable guidance in the Console and the PR template. Goals: reduce oncall escalations caused by malformed utilities, shorten remediation time by improving telemetry consistency, and provide a canary path for granting utilities to non-privileged staff.
acceptance_criteria: Inspector can parse and validate the taskified utility manifest and report schema mismatches with line-level diagnostics
Dry-run mode executes playflow steps in a sandbox and produces a deterministic execution plan without external side effects
RBAC analysis surfaces required permission scopes for every step and flags steps that require elevation
Telemetry linter enforces presence of standardized labels (route, model, customer_id|null) and fails promotion on missing critical labels
Console integration: a new pre-promotion check panel that shows Inspector results in the playflow detail page
CLI: inspector validate|inspect|dryrun commands with machine-readable JSON output for CI gating
Instrumentation: Inspector emits structured telemetry events and traces to the ops observability pipeline
implementation_steps: Design manifest schema extension to include explicit side-effect annotations and required telemetry labels
Prototype a sandboxed dry-run harness using existing admin-sandbox infra (containerized, network-disabled)
Implement static analyzer that walks playflow AST to compute permission footprints and KV mutation sites
Build telemetry linter with configurable rules; default rules align with Console's cost/latency tagging
Create a small REST service + CLI wrapper (inspector service) that exposes validate/inspect/dryrun endpoints
Wire Inspector results into the Console promotion workflow and PR templates
Add CI step to task catalog repo that runs inspector validate and fails on high-severity findings
Write exhaustive unit and integration tests, and run an internal pilot with Support team for two weeks
test_plan: Unit tests: manifest parsing, linter rules, permission analyzer, and CLI args
Integration tests: dry-run harness against 20 representative playflows (diagnostics, remediation, idempotent patches)
Chaos test: intentionally malformed manifests and simulated network errors to verify inspector fail-open vs fail-closed behavior
User acceptance: run three onboarding sessions with Support and Ops engineers to validate UX and guidance usefulness
Telemetry QA: validate Inspector events appear in Console dashboards and tie back to playflow IDs
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dev test on staging catalog (1 week)
Phase 1: Pilot with Support team; require inspector sign-off for new playflows (2 weeks)
Phase 2: CI gating enforcement for non-privileged catalog changes; advisory-only for privileged owners (3 weeks)
Phase 3: Full enforcement and Console promotion gating after pilot feedback and bugfix cycle
monitoring: Track number of playflows failing Inspector by category (schema, telemetry, RBAC, dry-run)
SLO: reduce playflow-caused escalations by 40% within 60 days of enforcement
Create dashboard: Inspector health, latency, and false-positive rate (from pilot feedback)
Alert when Inspector dry-run time > 10s or error rate > 3%
